factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for yelloweye rockfish.
factors.value_notes: WDFW, ODFW and NOAA AFSC sources document yelloweye distribution, climate sensitivity and deep rocky-reef habitat but do not establish a numeric preferred surface-temperature range. Climate sensitivity through prey availability is not a thermal preference curve. The configured 6-14 °C range and 8-12 °C ideal remain unsupported; keep values unchanged and mark needs_source.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for yelloweye rockfish.
factors.value_notes: WDFW reports yelloweye from 11-549 m, with adults typically 91-180 m and juveniles in shallower kelp/algal habitat; adults and older juveniles use deep, high-relief complex rock. ODFW reports 8-300 fathoms, and NOAA AFSC gives a common depth range of roughly 50-400 m. The configured 30-200 m band overlaps adult habitat but does not cover the full ontogenetic range or deeper occurrences.
